title: Maximum area of a rectangle with a wall as one side
sources: Test Form A #30 type (fence length differs)
OpenStax College Algebra 2e §5.1 Example 5 p. 398 (CC BY 4.0): method only
process_card: Maximum area with a wall as one side

problem.prompt: {P} ft of fencing will enclose a rectangle; a wall forms one side. Find the width w that gives the largest area, and that area.

steps.name: write the area as a function of the width
find the width at the vertex

answer.say: Make it {w0} ft wide and {L0} ft long (parallel to the wall); the maximum area is {A0} ft².

mistakes.name: fenced all four sides
mistakes.message: The wall is one side: the fence makes only two widths and one length.

mistakes.name: gave the length as the width
mistakes.message: The vertex gives the width w (the side touching the wall); the length is P - 2w.

hints.hint: Two widths and one length use all the fence.
hints.why: The wall is the fourth side, so it needs no fence.
The area has to be a function of one variable.

hints.step: write the area as a function of the width
hints.why: That gives a quadratic in w that opens down.

hints.step: find the width at the vertex
hints.why: The largest area is at the vertex.
The question asks for both dimensions.
That is the maximum value of A.
